title: Pay dispute with Hines
summary: Eckstine gets a raise to $25 a night, Hines refuses Budd the same, and Budd announces he is quitting in December 1942.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: So, okay, so we went on and we went on and we went on, so one day down in Hot Springs, Arkansas before we hit Billy Eckstein came to me, he said, okay, B, he says I just got my raise. You know, because we were supposed to make the same money. I said, yeah, how much you making now, he says Earl said I could make $25.00 a night. I said -- so he said 'you'd better go on down and get yours straight.' I said 'will do.' So I walked down into the dressing room and said okay, you raised Billy 25 a night, I want my 25 a night. He said 'I can't afford to pay you $25.00 a night, B,' and he says you know -- I said, 'Look Earl, don't tell me what you can't afford to pay, I'm looking at the books every night. I know every penny that comes in and what goes out,' I says, 'and you can afford to pay.'

He says, yeah, but Billy Eckstein is the star, he said -- I said, I wouldn't care who is the star. I said it was the agreement that Billy would make no more than me, I wouldn't make no more than Billy, and that we organized and founded the band, and I did all of the rehearsing, I'm writing the music and everything. I says, I don't care how big it is, I figure I'm entitled to the same money.

So he says, well man, I can't give it to you. I said, you can't give it to me, I said, okay, I'm quitting. So now this was in December of 1942 now. I jumped my story a little bit because I didn't bring in '41.
